about: Haus Klosterberg is the name of Markus Molitor’s home: the estate house that stands among the vines above Wehlen, in the heart of the Middle Mosel, renovated between 2009 and 2012 in a mix of old and new materials. Molitor took over his family’s winery in 1984 at the age of twenty, the eighth generation to do so, and has since built it into one of Germany’s most celebrated Riesling estates, with parcels in famous slate sites from Brauneberg to Traben-Trarbach and, since 2001, on the Saar.

This is the estate Riesling that carries the house’s name, drawn from steep slate slopes, some approaching an 80 percent gradient and all tended by hand. The grapes are picked by hand, gently pressed after a short maceration, and fermented slowly and cool with the vineyard’s own yeasts. The wine matures mostly in stainless steel, partly in large old oak casks, and spends an extended time on its fine lees before bottling under screw cap.

Molitor bottles Haus Klosterberg in a dry style and also in a sweeter, lower-alcohol version, so the capsule matters. Reviewing the 2023 at the estate, The Wine Advocate found a clear, slaty nose with hints of popcorn and cocoa bean and an elegant, fresh, structured finish. Slate is the thread through all of Molitor’s wines, and it shows here in the clear, stony nose critics describe. With its moderate alcohol and fine acidity, this is the house’s introduction to a style the Molitor name has made famous.
facts: Hand-harvested; spontaneous fermentation with native yeasts
